messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike in 5xxs (504/502) observed for inference-gateway-private-eu-west1 — 20m/5m ratio 15x baseline. Service error-rate > 10% for private deployments in eu-west1. Auto-page sent to #oncall.
jamie (oncall): acked. I'm on it. Paging netops + eng-infra. @sam @alex can you take a look? :mag_right:
sam (netops): jumping in. seeing a burst of ESTABLISHED -> RST from gateway nodes to external model endpoints. conntrack table for nat-gw-eu-west1 is near 90%.
alex (eng-infra): ouch. logs show a lot of ephemeral port exhaustion on the NAT appliance. kernel conntrack counts spiking. stack: private-vpc -> nat-gw-eu-west1 -> transit -> model-host.
jamie (oncall): impact? are customers timing out or seeing 5xx from our side?
maria (support): support tickets flagged: two enterprise customers (ACME, BrightHealth) reported timeouts and elevated errors in their inference routes. ACME has an ongoing high-throughput job.
sam (netops): running: ```sudo conntrack -L | wc -l``` -> ~230k entries (limit 262k). Watch: `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max` = 262144
alex (eng-infra): logs from gateway show `504 Gateway Timeout` from our proxy when upstream connections fail. Also seeing many `ERROR: short read` in runtime logs.
jamie (oncall): quick mitigation options: 1) increase conntrack limit on nat-gw hosts, 2) failover traffic to backup nat-gw in eu-west1-b, 3) throttle/limit high-throughput tenants temporarily, 4) fallback route to hosted model variants (no private egress). Which is fastest?
sam (netops): fastest is bump conntrack on current nodes + clear some stale entries. Can run sysctl and then restart conntrack helper. Doing: ```sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288``` -> applied on nat-gw-0/1/2
alex (eng-infra): I'll trigger a graceful drain of nat-gw-0 and move a subset of instances to backup nat-gw-1. Using route weights to rebalance.
ops-lead: note: dont restart gateway processes blindly, prefer conntrack bump + route reweight to avoid blastering tcp connections. also notify customers about potential interruption.
maria (support): I'll draft a short status update for affected customers and post in CS portal. Can someone confirm ETA for mitigation?
sam (netops): conntrack bump done across appliances. monitoring shows conntrack usage dropping after we forced a soft-evict on longest-lived UDP/TCP flows. Reweighting routes now: ```curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/route/reweight -d '{"route":"private-egress","weight":30}'``` -> in flight.
jamie (oncall): Alex, any change on gateway error rate yet?
alex (eng-infra): metric stream: 5xx rate dropped from 11.2% -> 3.4% in the last 90s. Latency still elevated for some flows. I see several pods still retrying and hitting backoff.
maria (support): pinging ACME support contact. ACME: "we saw a burst of 504s around 14:03 UTC, backlog of requests queued, some replays failed" — customer is reducing job parallelism now.
derek (customer): (via customer reply) thanks for the heads-up. We moved some jobs off the private route. Please advise when normal traffic resumes.
jamie (oncall): good. We'll keep mitigation until stable. Next steps: monitor 15m, plan a controlled failover to backup nat-gw if rate creeps. Sam, can you also check security group rules? sometimes ephemeral port range or stateful SNAT rules cause port collisions.
sam (netops): checked SGs: no deny rules. But I found a stale iptables MASQUERADE rule that only covers ports < 32768 on an older NAT node; newer clients using high ephemeral ports > 32768 were not being correctly SNATed. patching iptables and reloading kernel NAT modules.
alex (eng-infra): adding a small fix on the runtime level: update KV-cache connection pool to reduce concurrent outbound sockets per model-host from 120 -> 80 for private routes as temporary throttle. Pushing config to prod for private-eu-west1.
ops-lead: good call. keep rollback plan ready. record all change-IDs.
jamie (oncall): using the incident tags: severity P1, #affected-customers: 2 primary + handful smaller tenants. Action items: 1) monitor 30m 2) schedule postmortem 3) ticket ops change to make conntrack bump permanent or autoscaling.
maria (support): posting status update: "investigating increased 5xx for private VPC egress in eu-west1. Engineering has applied temporary mitigations; we'll follow up with timeline." :email:
sam (netops): final check: NAT appliance CPU is fine, conntrack back to ~60k. No new RST flood. Egress retries still slightly high but stable.
alex (eng-infra): runtime telemetry shows error-rate per-route 504 -> now 0.6% over last 5m. Rolling back temporary throttle on few non-critical canaries.
derek (customer): service looks good from our end. thanks team.
jamie (oncall): preparing handoff to night oncall in 48m. @ops-lead please accept handoff with summary.
ops-lead: accepting. For handoff note: root cause suspected combination of (a) NAT conntrack pressure due to high-throughput tenant + (b) legacy iptables MASQUERADE rule that excluded high ephemeral ports. Mitigations done: conntrack limit doubled, iptables MASQUERADE rule patched, traffic reweighted, runtime pool throttle applied temporarily. Followups: autoscale conntrack, bake iptables fix to golden image, run regression for private egress under high parallelism.
maria (support): created tickets: CS-4521 (ACME), CS-4522 (BrightHealth) and internal infra ticket INFRA-7890 for NAT hardening.
jamie (oncall): posting preliminary incident summary to #incidents-postmortem after stabilizing. If anyone sees reappearance escalate immediately. :rotating_light:
incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: page closed automatically after no new escalations for 20m. Record ID: INC-20260314-3729001111
ops-lead: thanks team. we'll do a full RCA and include mitigation checklist. closing thread when next oncall confirms stable for 2 hours.
